selected.title: The Venue Asked for My Fiancee's Divorce Papers
selected.hook: The wedding venue asked for my fiancée's divorce papers three weeks before our ceremony.
selected.voiceover:
The wedding venue asked for my fiancée's divorce papers three weeks before our ceremony.

Lena and I had been engaged for months. Invitations were out, deposits paid, and our wedding was twenty-three days away.

The venue coordinator emailed saying the county required proof that Lena's previous marriage had been dissolved.

Previous marriage?

Lena had always told me she'd never been married.

When I asked her, she went quiet. Then she called it "basically paperwork" from when she was twenty-two.

She and her college boyfriend had impulsively married at a courthouse. They split eight months later and never spoke about it again.

I asked why she'd hidden it.

She said it wasn't a real marriage to her and she knew I'd make it bigger than it was.

Then I asked to see the divorce papers.

There weren't any.

They had separated, moved to different states, and never filed.

So while we've been planning our wedding, my fiancée has still been married to someone else.

She says they're filing an uncontested divorce now and wants to keep our ceremony date.

Her parents knew. Her maid of honor knew. Even our officiant knew.

I was the only person who didn't.

Everyone says postponing would waste thousands over an old technicality.

But if it was really just paperwork, why was I the one person she couldn't tell?

Would you postpone the wedding, or forgive it if the divorce gets finalized in time?
selected.youtube_description:
Three weeks before his wedding, a routine venue email asks for his fiancée's divorce papers — except she always said she'd never been married. What follows turns a nearly finished wedding plan into a relationship drama about a hidden legal marriage, trust, and a secret everyone seemed to know except the groom. Would you keep the wedding date if the paperwork could be fixed in time?
